Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\git-cli-grammar-discipline.md:26:2. **`--` ends option processing; subsequent tokens take the command's post-separator grammar.** Verbatim from git-commit OPTIONS section: "Do not interpret any more arguments as options." For commands whose post-separator grammar is `<pathspec>...` or `[<pathspec>...]` (commit, add, checkout path forms, restore, diff, log, stash push, bisect start), later `-F`, `-m`, `-S`, `--only`, `--no-verify`, etc. are pathspec strings, not flags — they fail to match because no pathspec by that name exists. For revision/path-disambiguating commands (rev-parse, show, log/diff with revision args, checkout branch forms), `--` separates revisions from paths; use `--end-of-options` (invariant #4) when the thing to protect is a revision/object argument. Cross-impl evidence: libgit2 `git_pathspec_new()` (pathspec.h L84-L90), gitoxide `Pattern` parser (gix-pathspec/src/lib.rs L177-L178) — both implementations parse post-separator tokens as typed Pattern objects, never as flag candidates.

docs\cosign-verify-attestation-discipline.md:252:- **Accept a valid Sigstore signature WITHOUT checking artifact digest + cert identity against expected upstream** (Pattern A fix-forward edit #7 per codex T1 #7 prescription) — refuted: Sigstore signatures only attest "this artifact was signed by this identity at this time"; they do NOT validate the artifact is FROM your expected upstream/repo/workflow. Verification logic MUST cross-check: (a) artifact SHA-256 digest matches expected hash, (b) certificate subject matches `^https://github\.com/<expected-owner>/<expected-repo>/` regex, (c) workflow path matches `.github/workflows/<expected-workflow>.yml@` when known. Missing any cross-check = effectively unsigned.
docs\cosign-verify-attestation-discipline.md:253:- **Use broad `--certificate-identity-regexp` matching forks / unrelated workflows / user-controlled refs when tighter identity is knowable** (Pattern A fix-forward edit #8 per codex T1 #8 prescription) — refuted: open regexp like `^https://github\.com/<owner>/<repo>/` matches ALL workflows in repo including PR-checks workflows, dependabot workflows, fork-rebased workflows (if attacker submits a PR with malicious release workflow). When the expected workflow path IS known (e.g., `.github/workflows/release.yml`), MANDATE tightening: `^https://github\.com/<owner>/<repo>/\.github/workflows/release\.yml@refs/tags/v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`. Forbid org-only OR unanchored regexps unless explicit provenance documentation justifies (e.g., multi-workflow release strategy intentionally varies workflow path).

Verification MUST be DRIVEN BY DISCOVERED cert/bundle issuer and identity — NEVER pattern-matched against a 2-pattern OR 3-pattern allowlist. .claude\rules\parallel-session-worktree-isolation.md:115:   - **(c) Lockfile + O_CREAT|O_APPEND atomic-write for SHARED JSONL append**: open the JSONL log with `os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | os.O_WRONLY, mode)` where `mode` defaults to `0o600` (owner-only — per Round-5b T3 round-3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS trust-boundary finding on commit `c2b5dee`: `0o644` was world-readable and leaked audit-trail content (agent prompts, PIDs, verdict cite paths, `agent_id` UUIDs, T1/T2/T3 verdict bodies) on multi-user hosts. Callers MAY opt-in to `0o640` group-readable for shared-CI cases via explicit `mode=` argument + documented umask interaction (e.g., `umask 0o027` for CI runner) — `0o644` is REJECTED as default for any audit-trail JSONL). **Migration semantic for legacy files** *(Round-7 amendment per T3 round-4 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.91 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `df37fb1`; closes non-migrating gap caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE — POSIX `os.open` applies `mode` ONLY when `O_CREAT` actually CREATES the file)*: pre-existing files at `0o644` (created under Round-3-through-5 mandates pre-Round-6) RETAIN their world-readable perms after open, leaving the audit-trail leak intact unless coerced. After every `os.open`, the caller MUST: (i) read `current_mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.fstat(fd).st_mode)`; (ii) if `current_mode != mode` AND the file is owned by caller-uid, call `os.fchmod(fd, mode)` to coerce existing file to the mode invariant; (iii) if `os.fchmod` raises (`PermissionError` due to read-only mount, alien owner, ACL conflict on Windows NTFS, etc.), FAIL CLOSED — propagate the exception rather than proceeding with non-conforming perms (the audit-trail invariant is enforced everywhere or fails loudly). Document in commit body for any consumer applying this rule: one-time migration shell command `find .claude/state -name '*.jsonl' -perm /044 -exec chmod 0600 {} +` (POSIX) OR `Get-ChildItem -Path .claude/state -Filter *.jsonl -Recurse | Where-Object { ($_ | Get-Acl).AccessToString -match 'Everyone Allow Read' } | ForEach-Object { icacls $_.FullName /inheritance:r /grant ${env:USERNAME}:F }` (Windows) for legacy `mcp_health.jsonl` / `subagent_transcripts.jsonl` / `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` / `subagent_start.jsonl` / `worktree_lifecycle_audit.jsonl` files created at `0o644` per pre-Round-6 mandates. The `O_CREAT` flag ensures a missing log auto-creates rather than failing the first writer; **if `os.open` raises (read-only mount, permission denied, disk full), the exception MUST propagate — do not catch-and-ignore** (per Round-5 F-1 silent-failure finding). Take an **exclusive advisory lock** (`fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX)` on POSIX / `msvcrt.locking` on Windows); **if neither primitive is available, or if the platform does not enforce advisory locks (e.g., NFS without NLM support), FAIL CLOSED — raise rather than proceeding without a lock** (per Round-5 F-2 NFS-silent-succeed finding). **Windows separate-lockfile mechanism** *(Round-7c per T3 round-7b NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `48c49fb` caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE)*: `msvcrt.locking` locks `nbytes` from CURRENT file-pointer position, NOT the whole file like POSIX `fcntl.flock`. Under O_APPEND the JSONL fd's pointer moves on each write, breaking lock-release symmetry (LK_UNLCK at the new pointer would find no lock at the byte LK_LOCK was issued for). Round-7b workaround (shipped at `scripts/_atomic_jsonl_append.py:_acquire_lock(fd, path)` commit `48c49fb`): open separate `<jsonl-path>.lock` file with 1-byte placeholder + lock byte 0 of the LOCKFILE (no writes to lockfile means file pointer stays at byte 0). Module returns `lock_fd` for Windows callers to release; `None` for POSIX. **Lock-protocol rollout constraint** *(Round-7c per same T3 finding)*: when the lock protocol bumps (direct-jsonl-fd → separate-lockfile-v1, or separate-lockfile-v1 → separate-lockfile-v2-versioned), enforce single-version deployment for the entire concurrent-writer cohort. Old + new code locking DIFFERENT lock domains do NOT mutually exclude — concurrent writers can race even though each ALONE acquires its lock correctly. Mitigations (pick ONE before any concurrent rollout): **(i) transitional dual-lock**: acquire both old AND new protocol locks in series during the transition window; **(ii) runtime version-marker**: write protocol-version byte to lockfile + fail-closed on read-version-mismatch (FORWARD-REF for v2 lock protocol bump); **(iii) single-version cohort barrier**: coordinate cohort upgrade via deployment system before any new-version runs. Currently sss has ZERO consumers of `_atomic_jsonl_append.py` (FORWARD-REF wire-up Ships 2-5 pending per `tmp/wave22-orchestrator-salvage-jsonl-mode-bits-audit-2026-05-05.md`), so the version-skew window is THEORETICAL until first hook migrates to use the module. Future protocol bumps MUST honor one of (i)/(ii)/(iii). HOLD the lock across BOTH (a) JSON-encoding the record AND (b) the single low-level `os.write(fd, encoded_bytes)` — never use buffered text writes (`f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")` via Python file objects can split into multiple writes). **If JSON encoding raises (`UnicodeEncodeError`, non-serializable type), release the lock and propagate the exception — do not silently drop the record** (per Round-5 F-3 silent-record-drop finding). For records where **`len(encoded_bytes)` — the byte count AFTER JSON encoding, NOT the key count of the dict —** exceeds the platform atomic-write bound (≤PIPE_BUF 4KB POSIX; ≤512 bytes for Windows or treat the lock as the sole correctness boundary), reject the record OR shard via option (b) filename-namespace; do NOT silently truncate (per Round-5 F-5 measurement-target finding). After the write, `os.fsync(fd)` if durability is part of the contract (audit-trail JSONL needs fsync; ephemeral telemetry may skip); **if `os.fsync` raises (`EIO`, `ENOSPC`), propagate the exception — do not silently ignore a durability failure when durability is contracted** (per Round-5 F-4 fsync-failure finding). Use for SHARED JSONL log targets (`mcp_health.jsonl`, `subagent_transcripts.jsonl`, `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` class) where consumers expect interleaved appends from multiple writers and unified-view semantics are required.

Genuine-truncation branch: only call `INCONCLUSIVE-INCOMPLETE` when the last grep hits are prompt-echo / early-investigation AND `tail -200` ends mid-investigation with no final verdict — high line count alone does NOT imply completion. .claude\rules\multi-source-discovery-breadth-discipline.md:17:**Distinct source definition** (per Pattern A codex T1 Fire 29a prescriptions #1+#2+#6): A "distinct source" is a distinct **backend / data corpus / provider**, NOT a tool endpoint.
